Compares multiple visibility algorithms for symbol table construction and analyzes their performance.

# Purpose
This code is a script designed to compare different visibility algorithms used in symbol table construction for programming projects. It imports several modules and functions related to language specialization, symbol table comparison, and core parsing functionalities. The script processes files in a given project directory, grouping them by programming language, and applies multiple visibility algorithms to these files. It then compares the results of these algorithms against a baseline algorithm, which is the Depth-First Search (DFS) algorithm, to determine if the visibility maps produced by each algorithm are equivalent.

The script provides detailed output, including any errors encountered during processing, differences in visibility maps, and performance metrics such as computation times and speedup factors. It uses the `argparse` module to handle command-line arguments, allowing users to specify the project path and optionally select specific algorithms for comparison. The main function orchestrates the execution by parsing arguments and invoking the [`run_multi_algorithm_comparison`](<#run_multi_algorithm_comparison>) function with the appropriate parameters. This script is intended for use as a standalone tool to evaluate and compare the effectiveness and efficiency of different visibility algorithms in handling symbol tables across various programming languages.
